correctness.summary: A maximum matching compresses to a conflict graph whose independent sets are induced submatchings and whose cyclomatic number is no larger than that of the original graph. Deleting at most one endpoint for each nonforest edge leaves a forest, proving alpha >= ceil((q-r)/2). The tree and unicyclic extrema follow, and explicit whiskered path/cycle constructions attain them. Finite exhaustive checks agree.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Searches covered older strong-matching algorithms on trees, the Cameron-Walker equality literature, fixed-order counting of r-matchings in trees, Ramsey-type work comparing matching and induced matching numbers, and unicyclic induced-matching literature. No equivalent cyclomatic inequality or exact fixed-order tree/unicyclic gap theorem was located in the checked sources or the checked public archive.

value.summary: The result gives a reusable cycle-rank bound connecting ordinary and induced matching numbers and derives exact fixed-order extrema for two fundamental sparse graph classes, with sharp constructions for every admissible order.

limitations: Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an equivalent result may exist under strong-matching or 2-matching terminology.
The full texts of several older tree-algorithm papers were not completely inspected and remain the main residual coverage risk.
The fixed-order results determine the maximum values but do not classify every extremal tree or unicyclic graph.
The statements concern finite simple graphs.
